newsitem.title: USA: Fla. LUST bonds seen sashaying to market by autumn.
newsitem.headline: Fla. LUST bonds seen sashaying to market by autumn.

text.p: Florida Inland Protection Finance Corp plans to issue its first, and probably only, tax-exempt bond issue in late summer or early fall, state bond chief Ben Watkins said.
The issue's size will be between $300 million and $325 million, Watkins said.
The bonds have been nicknamed LUST bonds because their purpose is to fund cleanup of spilled fuel from Leaking Underground Storage Tanks.
The state legislature established the Florida Inland Protection Finance Corp to act as a financing arm for the program, which reimburses contractors for cleaning up the hazardous sites.
As a new issuer, the corporation must undergo bond validation by the Florida Supreme Court. Attorneys for the state Division of Bond Finance submitted briefs to the court last week.
The process is considered routine and state officials expect to receive validation before the court adjourns at the end of the summer.
Watkins said the issue probably would be the only one by the corporation.
"It's not going to be an ongoing program," Watkins said. "It was enacted to clean up a backlog of reimbursement spending."
The state has a backlog of about $500 million of reimbursement claims submitted by contractors, but has only about $100 million annually in fuel tax revenues to repay them.

The Legislature has revamped the program to avoid future backlogs. Under the old system, any contractor who cleaned up a tank site could submit a claim for payment. Under the new system, the Department of Environmental Protection has ranked the remaining sites in order of cleanup priority, and requires contractors to seek department approval before starting the work.
"They can prioritize what limited resources they have available, so presumably there's more control," Watkins said.
